extracted.intended_audience: general readers seeking an encyclopedic overview of Reuters (news agency)
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article giving a historical overview, organisational facts, editorial policies, controversies, awards, and related information about the Reuters news agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reuters Trust Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The Reuters Trust Principles were put in place to maintain the company's independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article states the Reuters Trust was formed and the Trust Principles exist to maintain independence; these principles are cited in contexts such as editorial independence decisions (e.g., partnerships) and are presented as foundational to Reuters' reputation and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards and Values (editorial guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Reuters journalists use the Standards and Values as a guide for fair presentation and disclosure of relevant interests, to 'maintain the values of integrity and freedom upon which their reputation for reliability, accuracy, speed and exclusivity relies.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a guide for fair presentation and disclosure of relevant interests; referenced as the internal normative standard that Reuters journalists follow to preserve reliability and accuracy. The page links this to protection of reporters and editorial integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy of objective / value-neutral language
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters has a policy of taking a "value-neutral approach," which extends to not using the word 'terrorist' in its stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editorial policy is quoted: "Reuters may refer without attribution to terrorism and counterterrorism in general, but do not refer to specific events as terrorism. Nor does Reuters use the word terrorist without attribution to qualify specific individuals, groups or events." The article contrasts this approach with other outlets (e.g., AP) and cites criticisms and incidents (e.g., CanWest dispute) that arose from strict application of this policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photo integrity and editing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters has rules about image editing and verification; after finding doctored photos it severed ties with the photographer and removed doctored images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: In 2006 Reuters was accused of using two doctored photos by a freelance photographer; Reuters severed ties with him and removed his photos from its database. The article notes Reuters' statement that cropping at margins is standard procedure, but it replaced cropped images with original ones when issues were raised and later "toughened rules after altered photo affair". This implies criteria: verify images, do not publish doctored photos, keep originals, correct/remove altered images, and enforce consequences for violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections and accountability practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters admits and corrects significant reporting errors and takes remedial actions when mistakes occur (examples include wrongly using an individual's image and publishing an editorial comment in an interview excerpt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article gives examples: Reuters admitted the error when an Indian man's image was wrongly used in a story and Reuters' communications director contacted outlets asking them to take down posts. In the Fernando Henrique Cardoso interview excerpt, Reuters confirmed the error and explained the comment should not have been published. Guidance implied: acknowledge mistakes, explain cause, correct the published material, and communicate with affected parties/outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters has set up social media guidelines for its staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page references that Reuters 'sets up social media guidelines' (citing The Guardian) but does not reproduce the guidelines. The presence of such guidelines indicates expectations for journalists' behaviour on social platforms (professional conduct, separation of personal views, etc.), and that these are formalized internally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership and content-distribution alignment with Trust Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters evaluates partner content and partnerships for alignment with the Thomson Reuters/Reuters Trust Principles; it removed TASS from its content marketplace when it judged the partnership not aligned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article recounts that TASS joined Reuters Connect in June 2020 but was removed from the content marketplace on 23 March 2022; Reuters' interim CEO said 'we believe making TASS content available on Reuters Connect is not aligned with the Thomson Reuters Trust Principles.' This implies a criterion for partnerships: partner content and relationships must be consistent with Reuters' trust/independence standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial independence in relation to funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Historic example: UK Foreign Office funding in the 1960s–70s to expand coverage, with the IRD acknowledging the agreement would not give them editorial control though they believed it would give political influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page describes an arrangement in which government funding was provided for expansion but notes the IRD 'acknowledged that this agreement would not give them editorial control over Reuters' while believing influence could flow through consultation. This highlights an implicit standard: disclose funding and guard editorial independence even when accepting external funding, and be aware of real or perceived influence.
